chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Why Continental and Columbia dropped Latin artists
summary: American companies lacked patience; there were hardly two Latin radio stations in New York, so records were not exposed.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Okay. Macho, years later on about 1954 - that's almost six years later - Tico Records - George Gomez- ends up with those Continental recordings and they are transferred to Tico. How did that come about?

Well, the Continental, like always, an American company, they haven't got the patience to deal with a Latin artists. First of all because all the records that was singing in Spanish, all the collections that they had with the disk jockeys that it was American, American --- In those days, I don't think we had two stations that was broadcasting Latin music in New York; and in Philadelphia, maybe one; and in Boston, one hour a week or whatever. So it was no chance to publicize, to expose what we record, so they discontinue. The same happen with Columbia. From Mercury we went to Columbia, with Mitch Miller.
